solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

definitions.meaning: a mark here is a check mark put against an item on a list
'just a ...' means just a moment, a very short time

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are everyday British usage: a check mark on a list, and a brief instant as in 'back in a tick'.

clue.text: Part of a church where patterns formed

indicators.note: formed means shaped, so the letters of patterns are made into a new word

explanation.surface: A section of a church where decorative designs were created.
explanation.definitionFit: A transept is either arm across the main body of a cross-shaped church.

clue.text: Beast arrived late at the start

parts.note: came means arrived

indicators.note: at the start points to the first letter of late

explanation.surface: An animal turned up behind schedule at the starting line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late at the start' looks like a time phrase but gives L, the first letter of 'late'.
explanation.definitionFit: A camel is a large hoofed animal, an example of a beast.

indicators.note: something phony is fake, so the letters of ringtone are a false version to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wonders which chemical element lurks in a fake mobile phone ringtone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'phony' plays on phones beside 'ringtone', but it is the anagram signal for RINGTONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogen is a chemical element, the gas making up most of the air.

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy
to appropriate is to take something for oneself, to steal

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that it is wrong to think stealing is fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe conduct that is unsuitable or not fitting.

parts.note: to rout is to beat soundly

explanation.surface: A team thrashes its rivals on an English golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A course is a way taken from one place to another, a synonym of a path or way.

definitions.meaning: a brick is old-fashioned British slang for a dependable, generous person
a fresh egg sinks in water while a stale one floats, the old kitchen freshness test

explanation.walkthrough: 'Brick' seems to be the thing that won't float, but it is a separate slang definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a decent, reliable person, and literally a fresh egg, which sinks in water.

definitions.meaning: hard-shelled fruits such as walnuts and hazelnuts
bananas is slang for crazy, mad

explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like an example of fruit, but here it is slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both hard-shelled fruits and, informally, crazy.

indicators.note: up-ended says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Vinegar almost tipped upside down gives off a strong smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks EGARNE inside 'vinEGAR NEarly'; 'up-ended' turns it upward, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To incense someone, stress on the second syllable, is to make them furious.

indicators.note: gripping means holding onto, so the song's letters close around the people

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera
men is a common crossword stand-in for people

explanation.surface: A country-and-western song that grips its listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country song' reads as a music genre, but 'Country' is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Armenia is a nation in the Caucasus, so it is an example of a country.

indicators.note: turned means twisted into a new order, so the letters of about are rearranged

explanation.surface: A submarine that has swung round to head the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-boat was a German submarine, so it is an example of a sub.

clue.text: Sauce sadly backfiring, tasteless ultimately inside

indicators.note: inside says that last letter goes within the backwards word
backfiring suggests going the wrong way, so the word for sadly is read backwards

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning sadly

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of tasteless

explanation.surface: A cook's sauce has gone wrong, turning out bland in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backfiring' turns ALAS into SALA; 'inside' puts S, the last of 'tasteless', within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a spicy Mexican sauce, often of tomato and chilli.

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical abbreviation for quietly
to refer is to send someone on to another person or place

explanation.surface: A discreet request to pass on a favour.
explanation.definitionFit: To favour one option over others is to like it better, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Naked king pinched by lecherous types?

indicators.note: pinched by means grabbed by, so the king is held inside the ogling types

parts.note: starers, people who ogle, with the question mark admitting the stretch
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A naked monarch is groped by lechers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starkers' is British slang for stark naked.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang word means wearing no clothes at all, a synonym.

clue.text: Epic thief goes wild for old coins

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of these three words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A legendary robber runs riot in search of antique money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes wild' reads as one phrase, but 'goes' belongs to the fodder and only 'wild' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: These were Spanish silver dollars, the stock treasure of pirate tales.

parts.note: ex means former, old, as in ex-wife
ample means more than enough

explanation.surface: A sample that is old enough to be examined.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen is one item taken as typical of its kind, a synonym.

indicators.note: End of points to the final letter of June

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: A flower festival held at the end of June.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian festival of the resurrection, an example of a festival.

parts.note: the one word names both a sausage and a loud firecracker, so a firework that is meaty is a sausage

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the word is slang for a sausage and also names a loud firecracker.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a sausage, the meaty sense, and an explosive cracker, joined in one punning description.

parts.note: gran is short for grandmother

explanation.surface: Give your old relative some time.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant something is to permit or concede it, a synonym.

clue.text: Comfortable thing, right up to this point

parts.note: a sofa is a comfortable piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Someone has been comfortable and right all along, until now.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means up to now, as in 'so far, so good'.

clue.text: Sounds like a mistake on which to stand?

indicators.note: sounds like says the entry is said the same as the word for a mistake

parts.note: a flaw is a fault or mistake

explanation.surface: A misstep turns out to be the very ground you stand on.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words sound the same in a non-rhotic British accent, where the final R is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: The floor is the surface underfoot in a room, what people stand on.

parts.note: was means used to be
p, piano, is the musical abbreviation for quiet

explanation.surface: An insect that once kept silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A wasp is a stinging flying insect, an example of the class.

clue.text: Greek character has not finished passing mountain

indicators.note: passing means going beyond, so the shortened word comes after the mountain

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain

indicators.note: not finished means the word has loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A character from Greece, mid-climb, has not yet crossed the peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passing' is a placement signal here: the cut-down word goes after the mountain, not a sense of walking by.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet, a character in that script.

clue.text: Plant, one no men adored, partly rejected

indicators.note: rejected says the hidden letters are read backwards
partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A flower that no man loved, partly spurned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' finds ENOMENA in 'onE NO MEN Adored'; 'rejected' turns it back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: The anemone is a flowering plant of the buttercup family, also called windflower.

clue.text: Comparatively fair offer in the end — less important to accept that

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the more trivial word holds that final letter

parts.note: pettier means more trivial, so less important

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of offer

explanation.surface: A fairer offer at last, though too minor to be worth taking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the end' gives R, the last of 'offer'; 'to accept' sets it inside PETTIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair can mean good-looking, so the comparative of that is more good-looking.

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: knocked over means toppled, so the word for the teacher is turned back to front

parts.note: sir is what British pupils call a male teacher

explanation.surface: A girl alone sends her teacher sprawling.
explanation.walkthrough: British schoolchildren address a male teacher as 'sir'.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris is a female first name, so it stands for a girl.
